title: Canonical recursive repository Module grammar
statement: Every governed repository MUST be a recursive tree of Modules. Each Module MUST contain README.md, contract.json, and at least one of code/ or mods/; atomic Modules MUST contain code/. Direct elements MUST be files beneath code/data/info/docs, child Modules MUST be immediate directories beneath mods/, code/data/info/mods documentation MUST be bidirectionally complete, and Fortress-controlled filesystem names MUST follow the canonical lowercase underscore grammar.
rationale: One recursive ownership grammar makes architectural containment physical, prevents hidden decomposition, distinguishes authored inputs from derived outputs, localizes verification with its subject, and removes arbitrary repository taxonomies.
failure_prevented: Unowned implementation islands, decomposition hidden under attribute folders, missing Module contracts, mixed authored and generated artifacts, detached test trees, arbitrary documentation taxonomies, stale ecosystem layouts, and entropy-producing path aliases.
applicability: Every governed repository snapshot using the Fortress recursive repository grammar. Formally recognized GitHub repository surfaces are evaluated as a closed root exception namespace rather than ordinary Modules.
evaluation: The Fortress core infers directories and Modules from the stabilized observed-file inventory, recursively validates Module structure, checks README.md, contract.json, and code/mods obligations, enforces flat attribute folders and mods-only child placement, reconciles code/data/info/mods documentation in both directions, and validates canonical filenames and Module names.

finding.message: An observed path or inferred Module violates the canonical recursive repository grammar.

remediation: Converge the path to the recursive Module grammar: keep README.md and contract.json at every Module root, keep direct elements in code/data/info/docs, place child Modules only beneath mods, add every bidirectional canonical documentation file including mods_docs.md, and use canonical lowercase underscore names.
valid_example: A composite engine Module owns cross-capability facade code and places standard_registry and snapshot_governance as immediate Modules beneath mods/, each with README.md, contract.json, and matching code/data/info/mods documentation.
invalid_example: A crates/ island exists at the root, a test suite is detached under tests/, code/ hides architectural subdirectories, a Module lacks README.md or contract.json, data/ exists without docs/data_docs.md, or mods/ exists without docs/mods_docs.md.
exception_policy: Only repository-level surfaces with independently verified GitHub semantics may be admitted to the closed root exception set. Ecosystem tools receive no general folder exemption; they must use supported explicit paths or surface an owner-level incompatibility.
history: Introduced during CHG-REPOSITORY-GRAMMAR-0007 as the canonical replacement for the earlier project-declared placement model.
Extended to require one Module contract and bidirectional mods_docs.md decomposition documentation.
Recognizes root .gitattributes as GitHub-supported integration authority needed to preserve canonical LF contract bytes across platforms.
